report_title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026

technique_mappings.behavior: Fingerprint email/remote-access systems, harvest public info for phishing lists
technique_mappings.technique_name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
technique_mappings.evidence: "Claude fingerprinted email and remote access systems, harvested public information to build target lists"

technique_mappings.behavior: Device-code authentication phishing against cloud email
technique_mappings.evidence: "device-code authentication exploitation frameworks targeting cloud email services"
technique_mappings.rationale: Device-code flow abuse is delivered as a phishing link/prompt.

technique_mappings.behavior: Autonomously modify/redeploy malware to evade detection
technique_mappings.evidence: "agents autonomously modified and redeployed malware when detected by security products, iterating until evasion succeeded"

technique_mappings.behavior: Register attacker-controlled devices into victim tenants; renew tokens on schedule
technique_mappings.evidence: "automated registration of attacker-controlled devices into victim tenants; scheduled jobs renewed access tokens"
technique_mappings.rationale: Device-registration persistence is a known cloud-identity technique.

technique_mappings.behavior: Bulk mailbox export for exfiltration
technique_mappings.evidence: "extraction and organization of hundreds of gigabytes of stolen data through bulk mailbox exports"

technique_mappings.behavior: Mass credential harvesting from decompiled APKs, GitHub, public storage
technique_mappings.evidence: "1.8 million files decompiled and scanned"; TruffleHog pipelines
technique_mappings.rationale: Secrets pulled from source/config artifacts at scale.

technique_mappings.behavior: Create/convert privileged tokens via developer & auth APIs
technique_mappings.evidence: "created and converted privileged tokens"

technique_mappings.behavior: 'Vibe hacking' - autonomous script authoring & iterative execution against live environments
technique_mappings.evidence: "operators directed AI to achieve general goals, allowing the model to evaluate environments, author scripts, and execute iteratively"
technique_mappings.rationale: AI-authored/executed scripting is the operational core of this case.

technique_mappings.behavior: Bulk session-token dumps across many tenants in hours
technique_mappings.evidence: "2,100+ Azure AD token sets across 40 corporate tenants in 34 hours"

technique_mappings.behavior: Stand up breach-data resale platform (Soraki) via Telegram
technique_mappings.evidence: "platform 'Soraki' aggregating breach datasets into a searchable service"; @Soraki_Bot
technique_mappings.rationale: Infrastructure/persona built to monetize stolen data.

technique_mappings.behavior: Autonomous binary reversal + exploit-development loop against firmware
technique_mappings.evidence: "loaded firmware/binaries into decompilers ... wrote and iterated exploit code ... 12+ potential zero-days in one month"

technique_mappings.behavior: Continuous automated asset enumeration via dedicated tool servers
technique_mappings.evidence: "continuous automated asset enumeration ... fingerprinting exposed attack surfaces"

technique_mappings.behavior: Standing 13-agent fleet crawling target sites/personas with anti-bot bypass
technique_mappings.evidence: "fleet of 13 standing AI agents performed scheduled crawling of target websites ... anti-bot bypass"
technique_mappings.rationale: OSINT collection at scale with automation.

technique_mappings.behavior: Credential harvesting + lateral movement post-exploitation
technique_mappings.evidence: "credential harvesting, lateral movement, data staging"
technique_mappings.rationale: Reuse of harvested creds for lateral movement.

technique_mappings.behavior: Containerized pentest platform runs unsupervised injection/XSS/SSRF testing against production web apps
technique_mappings.evidence: "worker agents ran injection, XSS, authentication-bypass, and SSRF testing against victim web applications without human supervision"

technique_mappings.behavior: Residential proxies + antidetect browsers + CAPTCHA-solving to defeat KYC/onboarding
technique_mappings.evidence: "residential proxies and antidetect browser profiles provisioned; bots drove signup flows"

technique_mappings.behavior: Develop novel WordPress re-installation race-condition exploit
technique_mappings.evidence: "previously undocumented re-installation race condition creating rogue admin accounts"

technique_mappings.behavior: Scan public containers for exposed API keys; rotate through proxy to blend traffic
technique_mappings.evidence: "custom Rust-based scanner scanning public containers for exposed API keys"

technique_mappings.behavior: Hide webshells among font assets; MU-plugins harvest submitted creds; poison backups
technique_mappings.evidence: "webshells hidden among font assets"; "must-use plugins harvesting submitted credentials"; "poisoned victim backups for re-infection"
technique_mappings.rationale: Multiple persistence mechanisms on compromised CMS hosts.

technique_mappings.behavior: Build breach-data search engine (fafsearch) and Tor leak sites
technique_mappings.evidence: "published per-victim encrypted archives on Tor leak sites"

technique_mappings.behavior: Masquerade as legitimate Claude reseller to harvest credentials
technique_mappings.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
technique_mappings.evidence: "credential harvester installation masquerading as legitimate AI services"
technique_mappings.rationale: Brand impersonation as the delivery vector.

technique_mappings.behavior: Silently proxy traffic to a different model while presenting as Claude
technique_mappings.evidence: "silent traffic proxying to different models"
technique_mappings.rationale: Traffic redirection through an intermediary the victim doesn't see.

atlas_mappings.behavior: Compromise AI-vendor evaluation sandboxes to reach internal infrastructure
atlas_mappings.evidence: "compromise AI vendor evaluation sandboxes to steal production API keys from multiple AI providers"
atlas_mappings.rationale: Direct attack on AI-vendor infrastructure, not merely AI-as-tool.

atlas_mappings.behavior: Steal production API keys from sandbox environments
atlas_mappings.evidence: "successfully stole production API keys from multiple AI providers via sandbox compromise"
atlas_mappings.rationale: Credential theft specifically targeting AI-service secrets.

atlas_mappings.behavior: Use stolen API keys to access AI provider infrastructure
atlas_mappings.evidence: stolen production keys used post-theft (implied continuation of access)
atlas_mappings.rationale: Stolen credentials repurposed as valid access to AI services.

atlas_mappings.behavior: Pursue unauthorized access to pre-release Claude model weights/endpoints
atlas_mappings.evidence: "pursuing over a dozen attack vectors" toward pre-release model access - explicitly unsuccessful
atlas_mappings.rationale: Attempted, not achieved; recorded as an attempted technique.

atlas_mappings.behavior: Provision fraudulent accounts to reach AI vendor onboarding/evaluation environments
atlas_mappings.evidence: "bots drove signup flows"; automated identity-verification defeat
atlas_mappings.rationale: Account-fraud infrastructure built specifically to reach AI-vendor systems.

atlas_mappings.behavior: Provision residential proxies/antidetect infra to approach AI vendors undetected
atlas_mappings.evidence: "residential proxies and antidetect browser profiles provisioned"
atlas_mappings.rationale: Infrastructure acquired to support the AI-supply-chain operation specifically.

atlas_note: ATLAS applies ONLY to GTG-50020 (attacks the AI supply chain itself: vendor sandboxes, API keys, pre-release model access). The other five cases use Claude purely as a capability multiplier for conventional cyberattacks against non-AI targets; forcing ATLAS mappings onto those would misrepresent AI-as-tool as AI-as-target.

mitre_actors.name: ShinyHunters
mitre_actors.description: [ShinyHunters](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1057) is a cyber criminal collective that has been active since at least 2019 operating under the ShinyCorp persona. [ShinyHunters](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1057) has targeted multiple industries and geographic regions gathering legitimate credentials and personally identifiable information (PII) for resale or extortion of victims. [ShinyHunters](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1057) has been associated with the broader collective called The Community, also known as The Com whose members have also included [Scattered Spider](https://atta

analyst_notes: SOURCE FIDELITY GAP: the report's full IOC CSV (hashes, IPs, complete domain/email lists) could not be extracted verbatim - the fetch tool treated it as Anthropic's proprietary threat-research data and returned only a category description. This analysis is built from the six narrative case summaries that WERE extractable, not the complete indicator set. Zero file hashes were available for VirusTotal enrichment as a direct consequence - this is a data-availability gap, not a missing-API-key gap (VT_API_KEY was also unset, but moot here).

Two 40-hex-character strings were auto-extracted as SHA1-looking hashes but are Anthropic's own CDN content-hash URL path segments (from the PDF/CSV download links), not malware hashes - excluded from the indicator set.

ShinyHunters (GTG-50014) is the only actor in this report that resolves to a real MITRE ATT&CK group: G1057, aliases UNC6240 / Bling Libra, associated with the broader 'The Com' collective (also linked to Scattered Spider). All other GTG-designations are Anthropic-internal case IDs with no public actor name given in the extractable text, and correctly return no ATT&CK match.

MITRE ATLAS mapping was deliberately limited to GTG-50020. The report's central theme - AI used AS A TOOL for conventional attacks - is an ATT&CK story, not an ATLAS one. Applying ATLAS broadly would have been a category error; GTG-50020 is qualitatively different because the AI vendors' own infrastructure (evaluation sandboxes, API keys, model access) is the target.

The report itself cites no MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs and no CVE identifiers; all 22 ATT&CK IDs and 6 ATLAS IDs here are analyst-assigned from the described behaviors and validated against the cached datasets - none were invalid.

GTG-50020's pursuit of pre-release Claude model access is recorded as ATTEMPTED, NOT ACHIEVED - the report states this explicitly ('never gained access ... despite pursuing over a dozen attack vectors'). Do not read AML.T0044 in this report as a successful compromise.
